meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: Common Law governs Hong Kong SAR while PRC Civil Law governs the onshore Foreign-Invested Partnership formation

Arrangement between the Mainland of China and the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region for the Avoidance of Double Taxation on Income and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with respect to Taxes on Income

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: People's Republic of China Anti-Money Laundering Law (2006, as amended by the 2024 revision, effective 1 January 2025); Administrative Measures for Beneficial Owner Information of Market Entities (PBOC and SAMR Order No. 3, effective 1 November 2024); Measures for the Administration of Establishment of Foreign-Invested Partnerships (2010); PRC Partnership Enterprise Law (2006); Hong Kong Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615); and Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) Part 10 on the Significant Controllers Register

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Certificate of Registration of Foreign-Invested Partnership)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) or local Market Supervision and Administration Bureau of the People's Republic of China
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route only: PRC notary public notarization of the SAMR certificate, followed by a single apostille issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China for use in any Hague Apostille Convention state; consular legalization is never chained after apostille

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) for the FIP; or Hong Kong Companies Registry for a parallel Hong Kong vehicle
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular legalization route only, for a destination state not party to the Hague Apostille Convention: PRC notarial certification, authentication of the notary seal by the PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and final legalization by the consular office of the destination state; the Hague apostille is not substituted or chained

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution of Founders / Power of Attorney for Formation Agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founder partners and their lawful attorney-in-fact, signed before a PRC notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route only: notarization of the resolution and PoA by a PRC notary public, then a single apostille by the PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs; no consular legalization is required or permitted under this route

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Partnership Agreement (Limited Partnership Agreement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: All general and limited partners, filed with SAMR as part of the registration dossier
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular legalization route only for non-Apostille states: notarization of the executed partnership agreement by a PRC notary, authentication by the PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and consular legalization by the consulate of the destination state; the Hague apostille route is not selected for this instrument

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter (banking due diligence and good conduct letter)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: A licensed bank in the PRC or Hong Kong SAR holding the founding partners' accounts
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille route only for banks located in an Apostille Convention jurisdiction: bank officer's signature is notarized and then apostilled by the High Court of the Hong Kong SAR for HK-issued letters, or by the PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs for PRC-issued letters; consular legalization is not combined

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency and UBO Register Extract
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The Foreign-Invested Partnership's registered formation agent or the SAMR-access-only UBO information system
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular legalization route only: notarization of the UBO register extract by a PRC notary, authentication by the PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs Legalization Division, then consular legalization by the non-member destination state's embassy; no Hague apostille is attached

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before admission of any partner, and at least annually thereafter, the partnership must screen all beneficial owners, general partners, authorized signatories and intended controllers against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the OFAC SDN List and 50 percent rule, UK/EU and PRC domestic sanctions lists, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority sanctioned names, and global adverse media databases. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for domestic and foreign PEPs, their family members and close associates; where a PEP is identified, senior management approval, source-of-wealth documentation, six-month review and enhanced transaction monitoring are required. All screening results and UBO records must be retained for a minimum of five years and made available to regulators upon demand.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: PRC State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) online enterprise name pre-approval system and Hong Kong Companies Registry Integrated Companies Registry Information System (ICRIS) for any parallel Hong Kong vehicle
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: For the PRC Foreign-Invested Partnership, the statutory name structure comprises four tiers: administrative division plus distinctive trade name plus industry description plus organisational form, i.e., Foreign-Invested Partnership. The Chinese name must be in Simplified Chinese script; an English name is auxiliary and must be a phonetic transliteration in standard Pinyin unless an approved customary foreign name exists. The Hong Kong parallel entity, if used, permits English and Traditional Chinese names; the Chinese version must be a true equivalent of the English name and must avoid prohibited tokens.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within fifteen working days of receiving a rejection notice, the applicant may file an administrative reconsideration petition with the higher-level Market Supervision Administration, attaching the original rejection notice, the proposed name, evidence of acquired distinctiveness and any ministerial approvals

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Hong Kong Partnership Ordinance (Cap. 38), sections 2, 5, 14, 26 and 38; Limited Partnerships Ordinance (Cap. 37), sections 4, 5, 6, 8, 10 and 12; Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310), sections 5 and 6; Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615), Schedules 1 and 2; and the relevant provisions of the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622), Part 16, only insofar as any foreign corporate partner requires a branch registration in Hong Kong.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies Registry, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (14/F, Queensway Government Offices, 66 Queensway, Hong Kong) and Business Registration Office, Inland Revenue Department (25/F Revenue Tower, 5 Phillips Street, Wan Chai, Hong Kong).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form LP1 - Application for Registration of a Limited Partnership (Companies Registry) and Form IRBR/BSA1 - Application for Business Registration (Inland Revenue Department).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Hong Kong law does not require minimum paid-up capital for limited partnerships. The Foreign-Invested Partnership Deed shall fix the capital contributions. All client funds must be held in a blocked escrow account at a licensed bank; no escrow disbursement may be made except on dual signatures from the managing partner and the compliance officer after completing the Medium-Risk Enhanced AML review for ISIC 7810 visa advisory services.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF THE CN-HK FOREIGN-INVESTED PARTNERSHIP (FIP)

WHEREAS the Partners have executed the Foreign-Invested Partnership Deed dated [●] 20[●] and have agreed to form the FIP to carry on business as international student placement and golden visa residence advisory consultants under ISIC 7810; and WHEREAS the FIP has obtained name clearance from the Hong Kong Companies Registry and is ready to complete statutory registration; and WHEREAS the Board must ratify the capital subscriptions of the General Partner and Limited Partners, authorize the opening of banking and escrow accounts, adopt a registered office, and appoint statutory officers in accordance with the Partnership Ordinance (Cap. 38);

NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED as follows:

1. CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTIONS. The capital contributions described in Schedule A of the Partnership Deed are hereby approved and ratified, and the Managing Partner is directed to deposit all subscribed capital into the FIP capital account, with client funds placed in a blocked escrow sub-account separate from operating funds.

2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The Board authorizes the opening and operation of banking and escrow accounts at [Bank Name], Hong Kong branch, and appoints the Managing Partner and the Compliance Officer as joint signatories for all disbursements above HK$50,000 and for every escrow release, and each of them singly for any other authorized payment, with all wire transfers to be conducted by SWIFT and governed by the AML/CFT manual.

3. REGISTERED OFFICE. The registered office and principal place of business of the FIP shall be [registered office address], Hong Kong, and the Board authorizes the acceptance of service of process at that address by the Secretary/Administrator.

4. STATUTORY OFFICERS. The Board appoints the individuals identified in the Officer Schedule as Managing Partner, Compliance Officer, Money-Laundering Reporting Officer and Secretary/Administrator, each with authority to file all forms and declarations with the Companies Registry, Inland Revenue Department and Immigration Department, to sign client escrow instructions, and to procure each required operating licence.

5. GENERAL AUTHORITY. The officers are empowered to execute all ancillary agreements, to engage attorneys and accountants, and to undertake all lawful acts consistent with this resolution. This resolution takes effect immediately and may be executed in counterparts.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Entity Name Clearance and Execution of the Foreign-Invested Partnership Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Hong Kong Companies Registry - Integrated Companies Registry Information System (ICRIS) Name Search
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search on the Hong Kong Companies Registry Integrated Companies Registry Information System (ICRIS) to confirm that the proposed English name of the FIP is not identical or confusingly similar to any existing company or limited partnership. If the name includes restricted words such as Bank, Trust, University or Capital, obtain regulatory consent or avoid those words. After clearance, prepare and execute a Foreign-Invested Partnership Deed in English, containing the general partner with unlimited liability, limited partners with capital commitments, profit sharing, management authority, capital calls, client-money escrow, dispute resolution and dissolution. If any partner is a legal entity, attach notarized corporate resolutions and legal capacity certificates.
required_dossiers: ICRIS name search report
Signed Foreign-Invested Partnership Deed in English
Passport or corporate registration documents of all partners
Notarized corporate resolutions of corporate partners
Consent letter from the registered office address provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is unavailable, file an alternative name within two business days; if the Registry queries the deed particulars, execute a supplemental agreement and resubmit within ten business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the Limited Partnership and Business Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry (Limited Partnerships Section) and Inland Revenue Department - Business Registration Office (simultaneous filing window)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form LP1 with the Companies Registry Limited Partnerships Section together with the executed Partnership Deed, the Form IRBR/BSA1 business registration application, and the statutory fee of approximately HKD 2,120. The Companies Registry will examine the limited partnership structure to verify at least one general partner with unlimited liability and at least one limited partner, and after approval will issue the Certificate of Registration of a Limited Partnership. The Inland Revenue Department Business Registration Office will issue the Business Registration Certificate governed by Cap. 310. The business description must state International Student Placement and Golden Visa Residence Advisory - ISIC 7810 so that no manufacturing or industrial classification is applied.
required_dossiers: Form LP1 executed by the general partner
Original certified Foreign-Invested Partnership Deed
Identity and corporate documents of all partners
Signed Form IRBR/BSA1 business registration application
Address consent or tenancy agreement for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Companies Registry issues a Notice of Defects, file an amended Form LP1 within seven business days and pay the correction fee; if the Inland Revenue Department queries the business classification, provide a detailed services description and the ISIC code within fourteen business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Banking and Blocked Escrow Account Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Hong Kong Monetary Authority authorized licensed bank; Joint Financial Intelligence Unit for suspicious transaction reporting and AML/CFT monitoring
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open the FIP bank account at a licensed bank after obtaining the certificate of registration and the Business Registration Certificate, using the executed Partnership Deed, partners' identification, source-of-funds statements and projected transaction volume. The target payment rails are escrow account and wire transfer. The account mandate requires two-tier approval: disbursements below HK$50,000 may be signed by the Managing Partner alone, while disbursements above that threshold and all escrow releases require both the Managing Partner and the Compliance Officer or Money-Laundering Reporting Officer. For the Medium-Risk Enhanced profile, establish automated transaction monitoring, segregated client-money accounting, pausable escrow controls, and prompt submission of suspicious transaction reports to the Joint Financial Intelligence Unit. All partners must pass KYC before any funds are wired.
required_dossiers: Certificate of registration of the limited partnership
Business Registration Certificate
Certified Foreign-Invested Partnership Deed
KYC and AML forms with source of wealth proof
Board resolution authorizing account signatories
Escrow agreement and client-money engagement terms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requires enhanced due diligence, provide additional evidence of the lawful source of partner funds and a formal AML risk assessment within thirty calendar days; if the account application is declined, repeat the process with another licensed bank and preserve a compliance record for audit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Statutory Officer Appointments, AML Governance and Immigration Licence Determination
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry TCSP Licensing Office (if applicable), Immigration Department, and Hong Kong Companies Registry statutory filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After issuance of the Business Registration Certificate, file any officer particulars required by the Companies Registry, designate the Compliance Officer and Money-Laundering Reporting Officer, and adopt an AML/CFT manual aligned with Cap. 615. Because the FIP will provide international student placement and golden visa residence advisory services under ISIC 7810 and NAICS 541199, the management must determine whether services amount to regulated immigration advice; if they do, the FIP must apply to the Immigration Department for the applicable immigration advisory licence or engage a solicitor to sign all immigration advice. A Trust or Company Service Provider (TCSP) licence is not required unless the FIP also provides nominee director, registered office, or trust services; if so, a TCSP application must be filed with the Companies Registry and approved before such services commence. All officers shall sign and date the statutory declaration of due compliance.
required_dossiers: Officer appointment resolution and officer particulars filing
AML/CFT policy manual and enterprise risk assessment
Compliance Officer and MLRO designation letters
Immigration advisory licence application or solicitor engagement letter
TCSP licence application, if the scope includes trust or company services
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Immigration Department queries the licence scope, obtain a formal legal opinion distinguishing referral-only placement from regulated immigration advice and amend client contracts accordingly; if a TCSP application is pending, do not provide nominee or registered-office services until approval is granted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial, Environmental and Civil Defense Licensing Exemption Recordation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Environmental Protection Department; Fire Services Department; Buildings Department; Labour Department - all for exemption and general office compliance only
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the post-formation environmental and industrial licensing exemption record in the statutory register. Because the FIP is a pure consulting and intermediary services business under ISIC 7810, there is no manufacturing, chemical processing, assembly, or warehousing activity under ISIC 1xxx, 2xxx, 3xxx, 4xxx or 52xx. Therefore no Environmental Impact Assessment permit under Cap. 499, no Civil Defense fire permit, no industrial licence, and no dangerous-goods licence is required. The FIP shall nonetheless complete a fire safety checklist for the office under the Fire Safety Ordinance (Cap. 502), including fire extinguishers, exit signage and means of escape; obtain the landlord's structural loading certificate under the Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123); and maintain general workplace safety under the Occupational Safety and Health Ordinance (Cap. 509). The exemption record must be retained for at least seven years.
required_dossiers: CompletedEIA exemption self-assessment form
Fire safety checklist or Fire Service Installation Certificate for leased premises
Structural floor loading statement from building management
Occupational safety and health workplace risk assessment
Industrial licensing exemption record signed by the Managing Partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any authority issues a notice despite the exemption, respond with a formal scope-of-activities certificate and obtain a written No Permit Required letter from the Fire Services Department within twenty-one calendar days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - no industrial licensing authority; the FIP is a non-manufacturing consultancy under ISIC 7810, and the relevant administrative authorities for general business licensing are the Companies Registry and the Inland Revenue Department Business Registration Office, with the Immigration Department for any regulated immigration advisory activity.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable for physical or industrial licensing; however the FIP must hold a valid Hong Kong Business Registration Certificate and, if it provides regulated immigration advice, an applicable immigration advisory licence from the Immigration Department or must engage a solicitor for all immigration advice.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Department, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Not Applicable - ISIC 7810 consulting services do not fall within Schedules 1 or 2 of the Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (Cap. 499); no project profile, environmental impact assessment report, or environmental permit is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - the FIP has zero industrial wastewater discharge, zero VOC emissions, and zero hazardous waste generation; general office waste is managed under the Waste Disposal Ordinance (Cap. 354) on a de minimis basis.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for a civil defense fire permit or industrial clearance; however the FIP must maintain office fire safety compliance under the Fire Safety Ordinance (Cap. 502), structural floor-loading compliance under the Buildings Ordinance (Cap. 123), and occupational health and safety arrangements under the Occupational Safety and Health Ordinance (Cap. 509).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration of the People's Republic of China (STA) via the electronic tax service portal etax.chinatax.gov.cn, with telephone hotline 12366; where Hong Kong SAR-source tax matters arise, the Inland Revenue Department of Hong Kong (IRD) via its eTax electronic services portal at www.ird.gov.hk.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: For the foreign-invested partnership (FIP), file establishment with the local Administration for Market Regulation (AMR), attaching notarised and authenticated identity documents of all foreign investors and the partnership agreement. Step 2: Obtain the FIP Business License bearing the Uniform Social Credit Code (USCC); under PRC law the USCC is the statutory Tax Identification Number (TIN) and VAT registration number. Step 3: The AMR automatically transfers registration data to the STA; verify or complete supplementary tax registration on the STA e-tax portal within 30 calendar days. Step 4: Obtain the electronic tax registration certificate and digital certificate for e-tax filings. Step 5: If annual taxable turnover is expected to exceed RMB 5,000,000, register as a VAT general taxpayer through the integrated e-tax platform; otherwise remain a small-scale taxpayer with simplified VAT filing. Step 6: For each foreign non-resident partner, apply separately for a non-resident taxpayer identification number with the competent STA tax office so that allocated partnership profits can be subject to withholding or self-assessment; disclose the partner's home-country TIN to the FIP. Step 7: If a Hong Kong SAR branch, representative office, or separate entity is created, also register with the Hong Kong IRD for a Business Registration Certificate (BRC) and obtain the Business Registration Number (BRN); Hong Kong does not impose VAT/GST and no Hong Kong indirect tax registration is required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible: Under the Enterprise Income Tax Law of the People's Republic of China, the FIP is fiscally transparent and is not itself an enterprise income tax payer; profits are allocated to partners and taxed in their hands under corporate or individual income tax rules. For Hong Kong SAR tax purposes, the territorial source principle applies, so only profits sourced in Hong Kong are taxable; profits sourced outside Hong Kong may be offshore if the substantive control and key functions are located outside Hong Kong.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The PRC does not provide a check-the-box or elective entity-classification regime for partnerships; the FIP is pass-through by statutory operation and cannot elect entity-level taxation. No hybrid mismatch elections are available under PRC law. In Hong Kong, partners may assert an offshore claim under territorial source principles, but the partnership itself has no elective tax classification mechanism.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: PRC Value-Added Tax (VAT). Hong Kong SAR levies no VAT, GST, sales tax, or comparable indirect tax. The FIP's study abroad and immigration visa advisory services are modern services taxable at 6% VAT in mainland China; qualifying cross-border services and exported goods may be zero-rated.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: RMB 5,000,000 of annual taxable turnover triggers mandatory VAT general taxpayer registration in the PRC. Any FIP making taxable supplies in mainland China must complete VAT tax registration from the date of business licence issuance regardless of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Under the STA Golden Tax Phase IV system, all VAT invoices must be issued through the national integrated electronic tax platform. Fully digitalised electronic invoices (FDEI) are generated online with a unique invoice number and anti-counterfeit digital stamp, and invoice data is transmitted to the STA in near-real time. VAT special invoices require digital stamping and entry into the VAT invoice management system; API-based reporting is available to taxpayers, and abnormal invoices are automatically flagged for anti-fraud review. Paper invoice reliance is being replaced by the fully digital e-invoice regime.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Cross-border supply of study abroad and immigration visa consultancy may qualify for 0% VAT export treatment only where the service is supplied to a client located outside mainland China, is wholly consumed offshore, and falls within the statutory cross-border zero-rated service list issued by the Ministry of Finance and the STA. If the consulting service is not on that list, the supply remains taxable at 6%. For physical goods, zero-rating requires actual export and customs clearance from mainland China. For qualifying offshore digital services, the recipient must be a non-resident and the place of supply and consumption must be outside mainland China.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Bill of Entry) for the People's Republic of China
Bill of Lading or airway bill issued by a licensed carrier
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) issued by a PRC-designated foreign-exchange bank evidencing foreign currency receipt from the overseas client
Cross-border service contract or sales agreement
Evidence of overseas consumption or delivery, including client onboarding records, visa/immigration service status reports, and delivery acknowledgements
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: PRC tax authorities will examine the documentary trail supporting the 0% rate. If the export or cross-border service claim is unsubstantiated, fraudulent, or repatriation of foreign exchange does not occur within the statutory period, the VAT exemption/zero-rating is retrospectively clawed back with late-payment interest at 0.05% per day and a fine of 50% to five times the tax evaded under the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Administration of Tax Collection. Fraudulent export refund claims and false VAT invoice issuance are also subject to criminal referral under Articles 204 and 205 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) under the People's Bank of China for the mainland China FIP; Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) for the Hong Kong SAR treasury side.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The mainland RMB current account is de facto convertible for genuine service transactions, including the education-advisory fees earned by the FIP, but every inward and outward remittance is screened against the SAFE enterprise classification and the genuine-transaction principle. The capital account is not freely convertible: any foreign capital injection into the FIP from the Hong Kong partner must first be registered with SAFE through the settlement bank and credited to a restricted direct-investment capital account; the amount and entry purpose cannot be changed without filing an amendment. Conversion of those capital-account funds into RMB is allowed only on a payment-by-payment basis against approved business use, not as a free conversion facility. Profit remittance to the Hong Kong partner is a current-account distribution once the FIP satisfies the partnership tax filing, has audited or CPA-reviewed financial statements, and passes the bank's distribution checklist; the bank will look for unpaid VAT/income tax, a partner meeting resolution, and consistency with historic operating revenue. In Hong Kong SAR, by contrast, there are no surrender or convertibility controls, and HKD/offshore RMB can be freely used for settlement, which allows the HK treasury hub to concentrate liquidity while the regulated activities remain booked in mainland China.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the PRC trade-in-goods foreign exchange control regime, all export foreign currency receipts must be repatriated into China through a bank within 180 days after the date of customs export declaration. The mandatory conversion ratio is zero: exporters and service providers, including the FIP, may retain the entire receipt in a foreign exchange settlement account or convert it to RMB at the market rate, provided the transaction is genuine and supported by contracts, invoices, customs declarations or service delivery records. For the FIP's study-abroad and immigration advisory services, service-trade receipts are subject to the same current-account repatriation principle and are monitored under SAFE's service-trade verification system; no surrender or sale requirement applies, but any delayed receipt older than the bank's classification threshold will trigger enhanced due diligence.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Non-Viable as a regulated treasury rail for the mainland FIP. Offshore fintech EMIs are not licensed by PBOC or SAFE to open RMB or foreign-currency current/capital accounts for Chinese resident entities, cannot perform SAFE direct-investment registration, cannot provide the required capital-account payment-verification reporting, and cannot issue documents acceptable to PRC tax authorities. The FIP may use an EMI only for non-regulated ancillary Hong Kong liquidity concentration, but every substantive inbound capital injection, client escrow, tax payment, and FX conversion must remain on the books of a licensed Tier-1 commercial bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: At least one natural person with statutory partner/signatory authority must appear physically in-branch for the KYC interview when opening the FIP account in mainland China. Remote consular proxy opening is not permitted as a full alternative. The Hong Kong corporate partner's incorporation documents, authorized signatory resolution, and individual UBO passports must be notarized and legalized/apostilled; the bank may also require a second face-to-face interview for the controlling natural person before account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential shell or conduit structure due to pass-through partnership legal form and non-resident Hong Kong ownership in an immigration/visa services vehicle.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified FIP registration certificate; executed partnership agreement; registered general and limited partner lists; beneficial ownership schedule for all individuals with 25% or greater ownership; Hong Kong Business Registration, Incorporation Certificate, and CRS/FATCA self-certifications; passport copies and address proofs; organizational chart with ultimate beneficial owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk client-payment topology involving study abroad and golden visa fees, third-party remitters, agent commissions, and escrow releases without service evidence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid statutory license or regulatory filing for study-abroad/immigration advisory services; signed client service agreements; fee schedule; bank or attorney escrow agreements; AML/CFT policy manual; third-party payment rejection policy; transaction monitoring escalation procedure; list of approved educational institutions and visa authorities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP, and immigration-integrity exposure arising from clients routed through Hong Kong intermediaries or jurisdictions that sell residency-by-investment products.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written PEP/sanctions screening policy; real-time screening records for partners, clients, and beneficiaries; client source-of-funds declarations with bank statements; risk-rated client acceptance files; due diligence files on Hong Kong introducers; escalation protocol for refused or suspicious visa files.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistency between the pass-through tax classification, low explicit capitalization, and large cross-border wires could be reported as prima facie money laundering or tax evasion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PRC tax registration and recent monthly/annual filings; CPA-reviewed or internally consistent financial statements; lease or office proof; payroll and social insurance records; detailed cash-flow forecast for advisory and escrow activity; partnership distribution resolution policy showing taxation of allocated profits.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital injection from the Hong Kong partner must be transmitted via SWIFT MT103 (for USD, HKD, or EUR) or CIPS (for offshore RMB) to the FIP's SAFE-registered direct-investment capital account at a licensed Tier-1 commercial bank. The remittance must quote the SAFE FDI registration number for the foreign-invested partnership and use the capital-account foreign-exchange purpose code for direct investment into an FIP; any credit that exceeds the registered amount or lacks the registration reference will be rejected or held in a pending account. After crediting, a PRC-registered CPA must issue a capital verification report, and all onward RMB conversion or settlement must pass the bank's capital-account payment-verification checklist against invoices, contracts, and the approved business scope.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements will use SWIFT MT103 for service fees, university tuition deposits, immigration authority fees, and refunds, with each instruction bearing a genuine current-account purpose code and the bank retaining the underlying contract/invoice. Escrow payments will be segregated in a dedicated ledger and released only under dual-signature authorization plus evidence of service delivery or visa outcome. Commercial letters of credit are not appropriate for intangible consultancy services but may be used only for a bank-issued performance guarantee or standby LC when an overseas university or immigration principal demands security. Documentary collections may support performance-related shipping documents in ancillary education-supply contracts. Hong Kong transfers will clear through HKD/CHATS, USD/CHATS, or RMB RTGS, and all other jurisdictions through SWIFT with end-to-end tracking.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore RMB/FX forward contracts through SAFE-licensed banks, limited to genuine current-account service receipts and payments with a maximum one-year tenor and no net speculative open position.
Onshore FX swaps for same-day/spot liquidity matching of non-RMB escrow disbursements, subject to underlying trade/service documentation and bank approval.
Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) booked only by the Hong Kong treasury company/partner; NDFs are not permitted for the mainland FIP and cannot be used to circumvent onshore SAFE regulations.
Cross-currency swaps are prohibited for this service-sector FIP unless linked to a separately approved bilateral loan and fully documented for hedge accounting.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Renewal of Business Registration Certificate (BRC) under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Business Registration Office, Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the expiry date of the current certificate (anniversary of the effective registration date); a triennial renewal option is available
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Carrying on business without a valid BRC after expiry is an offence under Cap. 310; on conviction, a fine up to HK$5,000 may be imposed and the fee remains recoverable as a civil debt. The Commissioner may also strike the business from the Business Register.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month from the date of issue of the return; automatic extension to 15 August for e-filed returns lodged by an authorised tax representative for a basis period ending on 31 December (or 15 November for a 30 June year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing without reasonable excuse may result in a penalty up to HK$10,000 under Inland Revenue Ordinance s.80(2); an estimated assessment may be issued; additional tax up to three times the undercharged tax may be imposed for wilful or negligent default.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Employer's Return of Remuneration and Pensions – Form BIR56A (if the FIP employs staff)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month after the end of the year of assessment (generally 30 April); extension to 30 June for e-filed returns via a tax representative
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file on time may be penalised up to HK$10,000; intentional or negligent non-compliance may attract additional tax of up to three times the undercharged tax.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is mandated for a Hong Kong partnership under the Limited Partnership Ordinance (Cap. 321), the Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112), or the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310). A mandatory independent certified audit may arise only where the partnership also operates as a regulated entity (e.g., an SFC-licensed corporation, bank, insurer, or deposit-taking company) with sector-specific thresholds. By way of comparison, Hong Kong incorporated private companies are required to have audited financial statements unless they qualify as a small private company or a small private company in a group under the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622), which generally requires meeting at least two of three quantitative tests: total annual revenue not exceeding HK$20 million, total assets not exceeding HK$10 million, and employees not exceeding 50. Those company-law thresholds do not apply to a partnership.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Accounts submitted to the Inland Revenue Department should be prepared in accordance with Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS) or HKFRS for Private Entities (the Hong Kong equivalent of IFRS for SMEs), with a full Profit and Loss Account and Balance Sheet supporting the partnership's Profits Tax Return.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Hong Kong does not impose an annual UBO confirmation filing on partnerships. The Significant Controllers Register regime under the Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) applies only to companies and registered non-Hong Kong companies, not to partnerships. A limited partnership must, however, notify the Companies Registry of any change in its registered particulars (including names of partners and capital contributions) within 28 days of the change using Form LP2. Separately, the Business Registration Ordinance requires the business to update its registered particulars with the Business Registration Office. If the immigration/visa advisory business also acts as a trust or company service provider, it may become subject to anti-money-laundering beneficial-owner due-diligence rules under the Hong Kong AMLO, but it would not file an annual UBO return.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (recording partnership resolutions and decisions)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300–1,000 per annum for a Hong Kong registered office address and corporate compliance agent
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,000–5,000 per annum for a voluntary certified audit of a small to medium-sized Hong Kong partnership engaged for lender or investor assurance

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% standard Profits Tax on unincorporated partnership assessable profits; corporate partners taxed at 16.5%; two-tiered concession applies at 7.5% for unincorporated business and 8.25% for corporations on the first HKD 2,000,000 of assessable profit.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Hong Kong operates a territorial-source, no-VAT/no-GST/no-capital-gains regime. The Foreign-Invested Partnership (FIP) may qualify for two-tiered Profits Tax rates; foreign-sourced income is generally exempt from tax if the relevant operations and contracts are performed outside Hong Kong; qualifying IP R&D expenditure is deductible at 300% on the first HKD 2,000,000 and 200% on the remainder; no withholding tax is charged on dividend distributions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Profits Tax Return - Partnerships (BIR52) filed through the Inland Revenue Department e-Filing / GovHK e-Tax portal; non-resident partners may additionally be required to submit BIR54 (Non-Resident Person) or individual/corporate Profits Tax Returns for their assessable share.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual Profits Tax Return is issued after the fiscal year of assessment, normally due within one month from the date of issue; e-filing returns are generally granted a one-month extension. Provisional Profits Tax is payable in two instalments, typically in November and April, with the exact statutory deadline stated on the Demand Note.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full English name of the FIP, Hong Kong Business Registration Number, registered office address, principal place of business in Hong Kong, and date of business registration.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the exact business registration number and the Hong Kong principal place of business. A foreign-resident investor must not insert a Mainland China office as the principal place of business unless day-to-day management and client services are actually performed there. Retain the tenancy agreement, staff employment contracts, and client meeting records to prove the Hong Kong establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 - Nature of business and industry classification
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Principal business activity code, including ISIC 7810 (employment placement) and the study-abroad / immigration residence advisory commercial subtype.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Describe the activity as International student placement and golden visa residence advisory. Indicate whether a statutory licence is held for immigration services. If the FIP earns commission from Chinese education providers, the commission should be sourced according to where the negotiations, contract execution, and performance take place; failure to identify the correct source is a common audit trigger.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 - Date of commencement and cessation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The date the FIP commenced business in Hong Kong and the date of cessation, if any.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a newly formed Hong Kong foreign-invested partnership, the commencement date is the date the first client engagement or revenue-generating activity occurred. A backdated or missing commencement date is an immediate red flag; the IRD assesses from the actual commencement date and imposes late filing penalties for prior years.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 - Basis period and assessable profits / adjusted losses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Year of assessment, basis period, net profits or adjusted loss before partner allocation, and accounting adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Hong Kong-source assessable profits. For cross-border study-abroad fees, allocate revenue on a transactional basis if negotiation and performance are split between China and Hong Kong. Claim offshore income exclusion only if all substantial operations and essential decisions occur outside Hong Kong; a mere formal shift of invoices to the partnership will be disregarded.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of assessable profits among the general and limited partners, including each non-resident partner's share.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Because the FIP is pass-through, the partnership return is not itself the final tax charge; each partner pays Profits Tax on their share. State the tax residence of each partner and the Hong Kong tax rate used (15% for individuals, 16.5% for corporate partners). A non-resident partner is chargeable only on the share attributable to Hong Kong-source profits and must obtain a Certificate of Resident Status if treaty relief is needed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Deductions, disallowable expenses and capital allowances
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedule of deductible operating costs, depreciation/capital allowances, interest, rent, and disallowable expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany management fees, escrow charges, and referral commissions paid to related parties must satisfy the arm's-length test under the Hong Kong transfer pricing rules. Add back entertainment and private expenses; deduct genuine employee salaries, office rent, professional fees, and bad debts. Keep contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation if related-party expenses exceed the statutory threshold.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 - Non-resident declarations and treaty relief
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of tax residence, absence or presence of a Hong Kong permanent establishment, and any DTA relief claimed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If a partner or external licensor claims the Hong Kong-China Tax Arrangement, attach the completed Certificate of Resident Status from the IRD, a beneficial ownership statement, and supporting substance proof. Where royalties are paid to a non-resident, complete the withholding schedule and remit the statutory withholding to the IRD before repatriation; failure to do so exposes the payer to personal recovery.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of BIR52 triggers an estimated assessment and a 5% additional tax; a repeated failure may raise the additional tax to 10%. Filing a false return is punishable under Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112) s.82 with a fine of HKD 50,000 and three times the tax undercharged, and on indictment imprisonment for three years; the IRD may also impose civil penalties of up to 100% or 200% of the deficient tax; directors and managing general partners are jointly liable for the partnership's defaults.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% - Hong Kong does not impose withholding tax on dividends or partnership profit distributions; no statutory dividend WHT arises on repatriation from the FIP to a non-resident partner.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: No dividend treaty withholding claim is required where no domestic WHT exists. For interest and royalties treated as Hong Kong-source, the beneficial owner must obtain an IRD Certificate of Resident Status (usual form IR1313A), furnish a beneficial ownership declaration, provide audited accounts / employment and premises evidence proving economic substance, and submit the DTA claim before or on the relevant tax return. Under the Mainland-China/Hong Kong Arrangement, the source state may retain 7% on interest and royalties, and 5% or 10% on dividends depending on shareholding, but Hong Kong does not mechanically withhold at those rates unless domestic law imposes the charge.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic royalty withholding for a non-resident licensor is an effective 4.95% of gross royalties, calculated as 16.5% Profits Tax on the deemed 30% assessable profit under IRO s.21A; the treaty rate under the China-HK Arrangement is 7% of gross royalties. Interest paid to a non-resident carries no general domestic withholding unless the interest has a Hong Kong source and is assessable to Profits Tax; the treaty rate for beneficial owners is 7% under the Mainland-HK Arrangement, while excessive thin-capitalised interest may be denied under arm's-length transfer pricing rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: HKD 4.5 billion group consolidated revenue for CbC reporting; HKD 400 million annual turnover for the Hong Kong entity and related-party transactions exceeding HKD 220 million for goods, HKD 110 million for financial/intangible property transactions, or HKD 44 million for other related-party services such as management fees and referral commissions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Hong Kong does not adopt the Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations, but the IRD applies a robust economic substance doctrine through IRO s.61 (sham), s.61A (general anti-abuse rule), and the OECD principal purpose test in tax treaties. For a study-abroad/golden visa FIP, the core income-generating activities (CIGA) are client sourcing, suitability assessment, visa strategy, contract execution, and post-landing advisory support; these must be actively performed by Hong Kong-located officers if the entity is to be recognised as a Hong Kong resident and is to enjoy treaty protection. A mailbox office with no local employees, no substantive board or partner meetings, and no local records will be pierced.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion by artificial offshore profit diversion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The FIP books all study-abroad and golden visa service fees as China-source or offshore-source income while the partners negotiate, settle, and deliver services in Hong Kong; referral commissions are paid to a zero-tax BVI shell and no economic value is performed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Inland Revenue Ordinance (Cap. 112) s.82 - fraudulent tax evasion is punishable by a fine of HKD 50,000, imprisonment for three years, and an additional tax liability of three times the undercharged tax; s.80 and s.82A provide civil penalties of 50%, 100%, or 200% of the tax deficiency depending on conduct.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The court may pierce the corporate/partnership veil and treat the controlling director or managing general partner as the person who knowingly furnished false tax returns. The individual faces civil asset restitution, freezing orders, a travel ban / blacklisting by the Inland Revenue Department, disqualification from acting as a director, and criminal imprisonment for up to three years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company abuse and treaty shopping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Hong Kong FIP is used solely as a pass-through booking vehicle with no employees, no Hong Kong premises, no partner meetings, and no economic substance, in order to claim Hong Kong resident status and access the Hong Kong-China Tax Arrangement on outbound interest, royalties, or dividend flow.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The IRD will disregard the shell under IRO s.61A and invoke the Principal Purpose Test under the Mainland-HK Arrangement and the multilateral instrument, denying treaty benefits, recharacterising the transactions, and imposing additional assessments and penalties equal to 100% or more of the tax avoided.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directing partners who sign declarations that omit material facts are personally liable for false statements under IRO s.82; the veil is pierced because the entity was a facade; the director can be blacklisted, prohibited from leaving the jurisdiction, ordered to make civil restitution of diverted profits, and criminally imprisoned.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The FIP processes client escrow deposits and visa fees through personal bank accounts, fails to conduct customer due diligence, maintains incomplete AML records, and knowingly submits fabricated bank statements or employment documents for a client's golden visa application.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615) creates criminal liability for breaches of customer due diligence and record-keeping, with fines and imprisonment; the Organized and Serious Crimes Ordinance (Cap. 455) adds up to seven years' imprisonment for dealing with proceeds of unlawful conduct; Immigration Ordinance (Cap. 115) penalises false representation with severe fines and up to 14 years' imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and general partners cannot hide behind the partnership: they face personal arrest, asset forfeiture, a travel ban and blacklisting, civil restitution to defrauded clients, and imprisonment of up to seven years (or 14 years for immigration fraud).
